summary: II active mḥasadle mene at 40/17 encodes the experiencer with the Preterit agent ending and the envy target with m-. This is not an omitted direct object inferred from the English translation.

III Detransitive maḥsəd at PrS 40/50 presents the sultan as intransitive experiencer, coordinated with mʕaǧəb. The stimulus is carried over from looking at Ǧawhar and his troops; no new government is proved by that preceding look construction.
Both passages already occur in the entry. Preserve II and III as filed; two contextual attestations do not settle the full dialectal relation between the paradigms.
No evidence here supports the revile/insult meaning mentioned in the etymological comparison. Existing etymology, glosses and p.c. material are retained without expansion.
Verify the reference mapping of inherited prs 110/7 to supplied PrS 40/50; identical wording supports identity, not an automatic citation replacement.
How do II active envy, II Detransitive envy and III Detransitive envy differ by dialect or coding? These two duplicate passages cannot determine the full distribution.
